items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
すし飯を海苔で巻いた太巻き寿司で、切ると断面に花や渦などの絵柄が浮かぶよう工夫がこらされる。芯や周りには卵焼きやかんぴょう、青菜の漬物、桜でんぶなど色合いの違う具材を配置し、一本の中に幾つもの色を仕込む。地域によって巻き方や絵柄に違いがあり、「太巻き祭りずし」「房総巻き」など呼び名も一様ではない。祭りや祝い事の膳を彩る、見た目の華やかさが身上の一品とされる。

## どう作るのか
すし飯を薄く広げた海苔の上に敷き、色や形の違う具材を計算して並べたうえで巻き込む。巻き上げる力加減や具の配置がそのまま断面の図柄になるため、経験と勘が要る作業とされる。太い巻きすを使って一気に力を込めて巻くことで、崩れずきれいな輪郭に仕上がるという。切り分けたときに初めて模様が見えるので、仕上がりを想像しながら手を進める。

## なぜこの形になったのか
かつては地元の名誉職の男性が受け持つ晴れの日の仕事だったが、戦後の暮らしの変化とともにつくり手が女性に移り、より華やかな絵柄へと発展したと伝わる。祭りや桃の節句、お花見、入学式など人が集まる場でふるまう料理だったことが、切り口の美しさを競う工夫につながったとみられる。年中行事や冠婚葬祭に合わせて各家庭でつくられてきた。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
A rolled sushi where vinegared rice is wrapped in nori so that slicing reveals a picture — a flower or swirl — inside. Egg omelet, dried gourd strips, pickled greens, and pink fish flakes are arranged by color at the core and around it, so a single roll carries several hues at once. The rolling style and picture vary by area, and the dish goes by several names, including "festival sushi" and "Boso roll." Its charm lies in the festive look of each cut piece, made for festivals and celebrations.

## How it's made
Vinegared rice is spread thin on a sheet of nori, and differently colored and shaped ingredients are laid out with the finished pattern in mind before rolling. The pressure used while rolling and the placement of fillings determine how the design turns out, which is said to take practice and instinct. Rolling firmly and in one motion with a wide bamboo mat is said to keep the shape from collapsing. The picture only becomes visible once the roll is sliced.

## Why it took this shape
It is said that men holding local positions of honor once took charge of preparing this roll for special occasions, but after the war the role shifted to women, who are said to have developed more elaborate designs. Because it was a dish served at festivals, the Doll Festival, cherry-blossom viewing, and other gatherings, competing to make beautiful cut patterns is thought to have driven its elaboration. It has long been made at home to mark annual events and family celebrations.

sources.title: 太巻き祭り寿司 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
九十九里浜で水揚げされるカタクチイワシを、ごまとしょうが、赤唐辛子で漬け込んだ保存食だという。地元では愛着を込めて「セグロ」と呼ばれ、青魚特有の香りにごまの風味と唐辛子のぴりっとした刺激が重なる、酒の肴にも向く味わいに仕上がる。黒潮に乗ってカツオやサバとともに回遊する魚を大量に水揚げする浜ならではの一品といえ、日常のおかずとしても親しまれている。

## どう作るのか
新鮮なイワシの頭と内臓を除いて水洗いし、塩で漬け込んで重石をかけながら余分な水分を繰り返し抜く。水が上がりきったところへ炒ったごまや赤唐辛子を加えて数時間漬け込み、二、三日ほど置くと酸味と辛味が魚になじんで食べ頃になる。漬け込む酢の割合は家庭や店によって加減が異なり、近年は冷凍品として流通することもあるという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
黒潮に乗って回遊するイワシが大量に水揚げされる一方で日持ちしないため、傷みやすさを補う知恵として酢と塩で漬け込む保存法が根づいたと伝わる。江戸時代に紀州から移り住んだ漁師が地引網漁を広めたことで漁が急速に盛んになり、一度に獲れすぎた魚を無駄にしないための工夫として、この保存食が長く受け継がれてきたとされる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Anchovies landed at Kujukuri Beach are cured with sesame seeds, ginger, and red chili pepper into a preserved dish. Locally called "seguro" with affection, it pairs the distinctive aroma of a blue-backed fish with the nuttiness of sesame and a sharp chili kick, making it well suited as a companion to sake. It is a dish unique to a beach where fish riding the Kuroshio Current alongside bonito and mackerel are landed in bulk, and it is also enjoyed as an everyday side dish.

## How it's made
Fresh anchovies are cleaned of heads and innards and rinsed, then salted and weighted down so excess moisture is repeatedly pressed out. Once the moisture has fully drained, roasted sesame seeds and red chili are added, and after several hours of curing and two to three days of resting, the sourness and heat settle into the fish and the dish is ready. The ratio of vinegar used varies by household or shop, and in recent years it has also been sold frozen.

## Why it took this shape
Anchovies carried in by the Kuroshio Current were landed in huge quantities but spoiled quickly, so curing them in vinegar and salt is said to have taken root as a way to make the catch last. Fishermen who settled from the Kishu region during the Edo period are said to have spread beach seine fishing, which quickly made the catch far larger than could be used fresh, and this cured dish is said to have been carried on as a way to avoid wasting the surplus.

sources.title: セグロイワシのごま漬け 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
アジをたたいて長ねぎ、しょうが、しそなどの薬味と味噌を混ぜ合わせた料理で、青魚の脂と味噌のこく、薬味の香りが渾然一体となる。粘りが出るまでたたくのが身上で、箸で持ち上げるとねっとりと糸を引くほどの食感になる。アジのほかイワシやサンマ、トビウオなど季節ごとに獲れる魚でもつくられ、素材の違いによって味わいも変わる。

## どう作るのか
獲れたての魚を三枚におろし、包丁で細かくたたきながら味噌と薬味を加えていく。たたけばたたくほど粘りが増して味がなじむため、皿にこびりつくほど仕上げるのがよいとされる。家庭でつくられるようになる過程でねぎやしょうがの薬味が加わったと伝わる。保存が利かないので、つくったそばから新鮮なうちに味わうのが基本とされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
房総半島沿岸の漁師が、揺れる船の上で手早く魚を食べるために編み出したと伝わる。しょうゆはこぼれやすいため味噌を使ったとされ、皿までなめたくなるほどうまいことから名がついたという説がある。漁の合間の限られた時間と船上という調理環境の制約が、たたいて和えるだけの簡便な形を生んだとみられ、今では居酒屋の定番にもなっている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Minced horse mackerel is mixed with miso and aromatics such as green onion, ginger, and shiso leaf, blending the richness of the fish's oil, the depth of miso, and the fragrance of the herbs into one. The dish is meant to be minced until sticky, taking on a glossy, almost stringy texture when lifted with chopsticks. Besides horse mackerel, it is also made with sardine, saury, or flying fish depending on the season, and the flavor shifts with the fish used.

## How it's made
A freshly caught fish is filleted and minced finely with a knife while miso and aromatics are worked in. The more it is minced, the stickier and better blended it becomes, and it is said to be done right when it clings to the plate. The green onion and ginger are said to have been added as the dish moved into home cooking. Because it does not keep, it is meant to be eaten right after it is made, while still fresh.

## Why it took this shape
It is said to have been devised by fishermen along the Boso Peninsula coast who needed to eat quickly aboard a rocking boat. Miso is said to have been used instead of soy sauce because soy sauce spills too easily, and one account holds that the dish was named for being so good one wants to lick the plate clean. The limited time between hauls and the constraints of cooking aboard a boat are thought to have shaped this simple mince-and-mix style, which has since become a fixture on izakaya menus.

sources.title: なめろう 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
房州産の海藻を干した「はばのり」を、焼き餅を入れた雑煮にたっぷりとかけた正月料理だという。青のりやかつお節も添えられ、磯の香りが汁全体を包む。黄褐色から赤褐色をした「はばのり」ならではの香ばしさが持ち味となる。産地から離れた九十九里や市原でも取り寄せて用いるほど、正月には欠かせない一椀として親しまれている。

## どう作るのか
冬から春にかけて採れる「はばのり」を細く刻んで簀の子に並べ、天日で乾燥させて仕上げる。正月には焼いたりゆでたりした餅を椀に盛り、汁をかけたうえで、はばのりと青のり、かつお節を混ぜたものをたっぷりのせていただく。地域によっては、はばのりの代わりに大根の葉を干した「干葉」をふりかける家庭もあるという違いもみられる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
見た目が不揃いで市場に出回りにくかった「はばのり」は、もっぱら地元の漁師の口に入る食材だったと伝わる。「幅を利かす」という語呂から縁起がよいとされ、年の初めに食べる正月料理として房総の家庭に根づいたとされる。地元でしか手に入りにくい食材だからこそ、産地から離れた土地でも取り寄せて用いるほどのご当地色が生まれたといえる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This New Year dish pours "habanori," a seaweed dried in the Boshu region, generously over a rice-cake soup. Green laver and bonito flakes are added as well, so the aroma of the sea fills the whole bowl. The toasted fragrance unique to this yellow-brown to reddish-brown seaweed is its defining trait, and it is prized enough that households even in Kujukuri and Ichihara, away from where it grows, order it in for the New Year.

## How it's made
"Habanori," harvested from winter through spring, is cut into thin strips, laid out on a bamboo mat, and sun-dried. At New Year's, grilled or boiled rice cakes are placed in a bowl and covered with broth, then topped generously with a mix of habanori, green laver, and bonito flakes. In some areas, households sprinkle dried daikon leaves called "hiba" instead of habanori, a local variation.

## Why it took this shape
"Habanori" was uneven in appearance and rarely reached the wider market, so it is said to have been eaten mainly by local fishing families. Its name is said to echo a phrase for "gaining standing," which made it an auspicious food, and it is said to have taken root in Boso households as a New Year's dish eaten at the start of the year. Because the seaweed was hard to obtain outside its home area, it is said to have taken on a strong sense of local identity, prized enough to be ordered in from afar.

sources.title: はば雑煮 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「コトジツノマタ」という海藻を煮溶かして固めた、正月のおせち料理だという。磯の香りが際立つさっぱりとした味わいで、醤油やかつお節、ねぎ、唐辛子を添えて食べる。人参やごぼうを混ぜ込み彩りを加える家庭もある。琴の弦を支える琴柱に似た枝ぶりから、この海藻の名がついたと伝わっており、銚子から九十九里にかけて親しまれている。

## どう作るのか
コトジツノマタをよく洗って汚れを落とし、沸騰した湯でとろみが出るまで煮る。とろみが出たら型に流し込み、冷やして固める。固まったら食べやすい大きさに切り分け、醤油やかつお節などの調味料を添えて供する。刻んだ人参やごぼうを加える場合は、とろみが出た段階で一緒に混ぜ込み、彩りと食感の違いを楽しむ工夫がされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
熱を加えるととろみが出て冷めると固まる性質から、かつては石けんや接着剤にも使われていた海藻だという。年末になると銚子の商人が正月用にこの海藻を売り歩いたことからおせちの一品となり、味の濃い料理が並ぶ膳の箸休めとして重宝されてきたと伝わる。小正月に行われる御歩射祭りで用いられる地域もあるという言い伝えも残る。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This New Year's dish is made by simmering a seaweed called "kotojitsunomata" until it dissolves, then letting it set. Its refreshing, sea-scented flavor is served with soy sauce, bonito flakes, green onion, and chili pepper, and some households mix in carrot or burdock for color. Its name is said to come from a branching shape that resembles the bridge of a koto, and it is enjoyed from Choshi down through the Kujukuri coast.

## How it's made
The seaweed is washed thoroughly to remove debris, then simmered in boiling water until it thickens. Once it has thickened, it is poured into a mold and chilled to set. Once firm, it is cut into bite-sized pieces and served with soy sauce, bonito flakes, and other seasonings. When chopped carrot or burdock is added, it is mixed in while the mixture is still thickening, for a touch of color and a different texture.

## Why it took this shape
This seaweed thickens when heated and sets firm as it cools, a property that once made it useful as soap or adhesive. Merchants from Choshi are said to have sold it around year's end for New Year's use, and it became a fixture of the New Year's spread, valued as a palate cleanser among richly flavored dishes. A tradition also holds that it is used in some areas during the Obisha archery festival held around the Little New Year.

sources.title: かいそう 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
アジやサバをたたいた「なめろう」を、貝殻や鉄板の上で焼き上げた料理だという。焼くことで味噌の香ばしさが立ち、ふんわりとした食感に変わる。ご飯のおかずにも酒の肴にも合う、香りと食感の両方を楽しめる一品とされる。産卵前の初夏に獲れるアジで仕立てると、いっそう脂がのって美味しくなるといい、年中出回る魚だが旬には格別の味となる。

## どう作るのか
あらかじめ十分に粘りが出るまでたたいた「なめろう」を、ホタテやアワビの貝殻、あるいは鉄板に詰めて焼く。じっくり火を通すことで表面に焼き目がつき、中はふんわりと仕上がる。よくたたくほど柔らかく焼き上がるとされ、たたき加減が仕上がりを大きく左右するため、下ごしらえの丁寧さがそのまま味の決め手になるという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
山へ仕事に出る漁師が「なめろう」をアワビの殻に入れて持参し、山小屋で蒸したり焼いたりして食べたことに由来すると伝わる。千葉の古い方言では家のことを「が」と訛って呼ぶことから、山の家で食べた料理として「さんが」の名がついたとされる。船上でとっさに生まれた料理が、山の作業場でも形を変えて応用されたことになる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This dish takes "namerou" — minced horse mackerel or mackerel — and grills it on a shell or a griddle. Grilling brings out the toasted aroma of the miso and turns the texture light and fluffy. It works equally well as a side for rice or as a companion to sake, offering both aroma and texture. Made with horse mackerel caught just before spawning in early summer, it is said to turn out even richer, since the fish is available year-round but tastes best in season.

## How it's made
"Namerou" that has already been minced until sticky is packed into a scallop or abalone shell, or onto a griddle, and grilled. Slow cooking browns the surface while leaving the inside soft and fluffy. The more thoroughly the fish was minced beforehand, the softer the grilled result is said to turn out, so how carefully the mincing is done ends up deciding the flavor.

## Why it took this shape
It is said to trace back to fishermen who carried "namerou" packed in an abalone shell when they went to work in the mountains, then steamed or grilled it in a mountain hut. In the local Chiba dialect, "house" is said as "ga," so a dish eaten at a mountain house is said to have taken the name "sanga." A dish born on the spot aboard a boat was thus adapted into a different form for the mountain worksite.

sources.title: さんが焼き 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
畑から掘りたての生の落花生を、殻つきのまま塩ゆでした季節の一品だという。ゆでたてはしっとりとやわらかく、豆の甘みと塩気がじんわりと広がる。炒った落花生とはまったく違う食感で、水はけのよい火山灰質の土地で育つ落花生ならではの、収穫期にしか味わえない味わいとされる。お茶うけのほか、おこわに加えたりすりつぶして和え物にすることもある。

## どう作るのか
鍋にたっぷりの水と塩を入れて沸かし、サヤごとの落花生を投入して四十分から五十分ほどゆでる。ゆでている間はあくが出るため水を多めにするのがこつで、三十分を過ぎたころから時々一つ取り出して硬さを確かめる。ゆで上がったらざるに上げてそのまま冷まし、サヤから取り出していただく。生のままでは食べられないため、必ず加熱してから口にする。

## なぜこの形になったのか
収穫したばかりの生の落花生は時間がたつとすぐに硬くなり味も落ちてしまうため、掘りたてをその日のうちにゆでなければおいしくならないと伝わる。火山灰が積もった水はけのよい土壌が広がる産地だからこそ栽培が盛んになり、干ばつに弱かった時代を経て品種を変えながら受け継がれ、収穫の季節だけ味わえる特別な食べ方として根づいたとされる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Freshly dug raw peanuts are boiled in salted water with the shell still on, a dish tied to the harvest season. Fresh off the boil, the beans are moist and soft, with sweetness and salt spreading gently through them — a texture quite unlike roasted peanuts, and something said to be unique to peanuts grown in well-drained volcanic-ash soil. They are also eaten as a snack, added to rice, or mashed into a dressed dish.

## How it's made
Plenty of water and salt are brought to a boil in a pot, and peanuts still in their shells are added and simmered for forty to fifty minutes. Because scum rises while boiling, using extra water helps, and from around the thirty-minute mark one is occasionally pulled out to check its firmness. Once done, they are drained and left to cool as is before being shelled and eaten. They cannot be eaten raw, so heating through is essential.

## Why it took this shape
Freshly dug raw peanuts are said to harden and lose flavor quickly, so they must be boiled the same day they are dug to taste their best. Cultivation is said to have flourished precisely because the region's soil is well-drained volcanic ash, and after a period when drought-prone varieties struggled, growers are said to have carried the tradition on by switching varieties — leaving this dish as a way of eating peanuts that is only possible during the harvest season.

sources.title: ゆで落花生 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
収穫した落花生を炒って砕き、味噌とともに練り合わせたなめ味噌だという。香ばしく炒った豆の食感と味噌のこくが一体となり、ごはんのお供にも酒の肴にもなる。家庭ごとに味噌や砂糖の配合が異なり、甘さの加減もさまざまで、同じ料理でも味わいに幅がある。学校給食で提供されることもある、日常に溶け込んだ身近な味とされる。

## どう作るのか
炒って砕いた落花生に味噌を加えて練り合わせ、好みで砂糖やみりんを加えて味を調える。甘さを抑えたいときは砂糖を使わずみりんで味噌をのばすと、まろやかな仕上がりになる。ごはんにのせたりお茶うけにしたりと食べ方は幅広く、多めにつくって瓶などに入れ、常備菜として保存しておく家庭も少なくなく、味噌の銘柄によっても風味が変わる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
市場に出しにくい規格外の落花生を無駄にしないため、農家がなめ味噌に仕立てたことが始まりと伝わる。冷蔵の手段が乏しかった時代、脂質やたんぱく質を豊富に含む落花生を保存食に変える工夫として広まったとされ、収穫地ならではの知恵と工夫が一皿の形になっている。掘り起こした豆を積み上げて乾かす光景も、この地方の秋の暮らしを映す。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Roasted, crushed peanuts are worked into a thick miso paste, a savory spread. The texture of the toasted peanuts and the depth of the miso come together into one, making it good over rice or as a companion to sake. The ratio of miso to sugar differs from household to household, so sweetness varies, giving the same dish a real range of flavor; it is also served in school lunches, a taste woven into everyday life.

## How it's made
Roasted and crushed peanuts are mixed with miso and kneaded together, then sweetened with sugar or mirin to taste. To keep it from being too sweet, mirin alone can be used to thin the miso instead of sugar, giving a mellower result. It is eaten over rice or as a snack in many ways, and many households make a larger batch, keep it in a jar, and treat it as a pantry staple, with flavor also shifting by brand of miso used.

## Why it took this shape
It is said to have begun when farmers turned peanuts too irregular to sell at market into this paste rather than waste them. In an age with little means of refrigeration, turning peanuts — rich in fat and protein — into a preserved food is said to have spread as a practical solution, so the dish embodies the ingenuity of a peanut-growing region. The autumn sight of dug-up peanuts stacked to dry also reflects the rhythm of local life.

sources.title: 落花生みそ 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
うるち米を粉にせず二度蒸してから臼と杵でついた餅で、もち米を使わないため粘りが少なくなめらかな食感になる。のどに詰まりにくく、汁物に入れても溶けにくいという扱いやすさが特徴で、米どころの家庭で親しまれてきた。別名「つきぬきもち」とも呼ばれ、道徳と経済の調和を説いた学問にちなんで名づけられたと伝わる。

## どう作るのか
うるち米をといでから二度蒸し、熱いうちに臼と杵でつく。もち米の餅と同じ要領でつきながらも、うるち米ゆえに伸びやすさは抑えられ、時間がたっても硬くなりにくい。汁物や鍋、炒め物、白玉風のデザートなど幅広い料理に加工しやすいのも扱いやすさの一因とされ、餅つき機を使ってつくられることも多く、家庭でも比較的手軽に仕込める。

## なぜこの形になったのか
江戸時代末期、高価なもち米を買えない農民にも餅のようなものを味わってもらいたいという思いから、農民指導者がうるち米で餅をつく方法を考え出したと伝わる。もち米の餅より硬くなりにくいことから保存にも向き、米どころだった地域の農家を中心に代々受け継がれてきたとされ、今も女性たちの手でつくり継がれながら地元の食卓に並んでいる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Non-glutinous rice is steamed twice without being ground into flour, then pounded with a mortar and pestle into a rice cake. Without glutinous rice, it turns out less sticky and smoother in texture. It is prized for not catching in the throat and for holding its shape in soup, and it became a favorite in rice-growing households, also known by the name "tsukinuki mochi," said to be named after a school of thought teaching balance between morality and livelihood.

## How it's made
Non-glutinous rice is washed, steamed twice, and pounded while still hot with a mortar and pestle. It is pounded the same way as glutinous rice cake, but because it is non-glutinous it stretches less and stays soft rather than hardening over time. This ease of handling is also said to come from how well it works in soups, hotpots, stir-fries, or even a dumpling-style dessert, and it is often made with a rice-cake machine, letting households prepare it fairly easily.

## Why it took this shape
In the late Edo period, a farming instructor is said to have devised a way to pound rice cake from non-glutinous rice so that farmers who could not afford the costly glutinous rice could still enjoy something like it. Because it hardens less than glutinous rice cake, it also suits preservation, and it is said to have been passed down for generations mainly among farming families in a rice-growing area, still made by hand by local women and served at the table today.

sources.title: 性学もち 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
あさりを蒸かした汁に味噌を溶かした汁物で、あさりの旨みと磯の香りが溶け込んだ味噌汁だという。椀にあさりを山盛りに盛り、出汁を張っていただく。身の大きなあさりがふんだんに獲れた海辺ならではの一品で、素朴ながら滋味深い味わいが持ち味であり、あさりの旬である春と秋にだけ楽しめる季節限定の汁物として親しまれてきた。

## どう作るのか
砂抜きしたあさりを昆布だしに入れて沸かし、口が開いて出汁が出たところへ少量の味噌を溶き入れる。あさりを椀に山盛りにして味噌汁を注ぎ、あさりの旨みが溶け込んだ汁ごと味わう。味噌は多く入れすぎず、あさり本来の出汁の風味を活かす加減が求められ、貝の出汁を生かすための塩梅は家庭や店によって少しずつ異なるという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
冷蔵の手段がなかった時代、漁師はあさりを蒸かしてから輸送しており、その蒸かし汁に当時貴重だった味噌を少量加えて賄いとして食べたことに由来すると伝わる。魚介が豊富に獲れる浦だからこそ生まれた、漁師の暮らしに根ざした簡素な味わいが今に受け継がれ、あさりの旬にあわせて今も地域の家庭の食卓にのぼり続けている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This soup dissolves miso into the broth left from steaming clams, a miso soup infused with clam umami and the scent of the sea. Clams are piled high in a bowl and the broth poured over them. It is a dish unique to a coast where large, plump clams were caught in abundance, simple yet deeply savory, and it has long been enjoyed as a seasonal soup possible only in the clam seasons of spring and autumn.

## How it's made
Clams that have been purged of sand are put into kelp broth and brought to a boil, and once their shells open and their broth is released, a small amount of miso is stirred in. Clams are piled high in a bowl and the miso soup poured over them, so the broth carrying the clams' umami is drunk along with them. The miso should not be overdone, since the point is to let the clams' own broth shine, and the balance struck for that varies a little by household or shop.

## Why it took this shape
In an age without refrigeration, fishermen are said to have steamed clams before shipping them, then added a small amount of miso — precious at the time — to the leftover steaming liquid and eaten it as a meal among themselves. Born in a bay where seafood was caught in abundance, this simple flavor rooted in fishermen's daily life is said to have carried on, still appearing at local family tables whenever clams are in season.

sources.title: ふうかし 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
クジラ肉をしょうゆや酒、しょうがを合わせたたれに漬け込み、生乾きになるまで干した保存食だという。見た目は炭や木の皮のように真っ黒で、炙るとたれの香ばしさとクジラ肉特有の風味が立ちのぼる。噛むほどに味わいが増す、酒の肴にもご飯のおかずにもなる一品で、薄くそぎ切りにして炙りながらゆっくり味わうのが一般的とされる。

## どう作るのか
クジラ肉をしょうゆと酒、しょうがを合わせたたれに漬け、味を染み込ませる。たれから引き上げて生乾き程度まで干し上げ、食べる際に火であぶる。香ばしく焙られることで、たれの香りと肉の風味が引き立ち、薄くそぎ切りにしていただくことが多く、噛むほどに滋味が広がる、しっかりとした噛みごたえのある仕上がりになる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
冷蔵庫のない時代、頻繁に食卓に並んだクジラ肉を長く保存するための工夫として、たれに漬けて干す方法が根づいたと伝わる。深く潜る性質を持つ種類のクジラを突き取る漁法で捕えてきた地域だからこそ、その漁の暮らしとともにこの保存法が受け継がれ、遠方に移り住んだ人が里帰りのたびに買い求める望郷の味にもなっている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Whale meat is soaked in a sauce of soy sauce, sake, and ginger, then dried until only half-dry, making a preserved food. It looks jet black, like charcoal or tree bark, and grilling releases the toasted aroma of the sauce along with the meat's distinctive flavor. The more it is chewed, the more flavor comes through, and it works as a companion to sake or a side for rice, usually sliced thin and savored slowly while being grilled.

## How it's made
Whale meat is soaked in a sauce of soy sauce, sake, and ginger so the flavor soaks in. It is lifted out of the sauce and dried until only half-dry, then grilled over a flame just before eating. Toasting over the flame brings out the aroma of the sauce along with the meat's flavor, and it is usually sliced thin, chewy and full of savor with every bite.

## Why it took this shape
In an age without refrigerators, whale meat that once appeared frequently at the table is said to have been preserved by soaking it in sauce and drying it, a way to make it last. Because this is a region that has long hunted a deep-diving species of whale by harpoon rather than net, this preservation method is said to have been carried on alongside that way of fishing, and it has become a taste of home that people who moved away buy whenever they return.

sources.title: くじらのたれ 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
イワシのすり身を味噌で味つけしただんごと、大根、人参、里芋を煮込んだ汁物だという。青魚のすり身ならではの旨みと味噌のこくが溶け出した汁に、根菜のほくほくとした食感が加わる。体の芯から温まる、寒い時期にうれしい一杯として、冬の食卓に欠かせない存在になっている。学校給食にも取り入れられ、幅広い世代に親しまれている。

## どう作るのか
三枚におろしたイワシを粗くたたいてすり鉢ですり、すりおろした長いもと溶き卵、味噌を加えてさらにすり混ぜる。大根と人参を煮立てた鍋に里芋を加え、すったイワシをスプーン二本でだんご状にまとめて落とし入れて煮る。だんごが浮き上がってきたら火が通った合図で、醤油で味をととのえ、仕上げに長ねぎを散らして火を止め、湯気が立つうちに食卓へ運ぶ。

## なぜこの形になったのか
九十九里の浜では古くからイワシが大量に水揚げされ、「海の米」にたとえられるほど食卓に欠かせない魚だったと伝わる。冬に脂がのる背黒イワシを余さず活用する知恵として、すり身をだんごにして汁に仕立てる食べ方が根づき、親から子へと受け継がれる冬の定番として、今も各家庭の台所や学校給食を通じて受け継がれている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This soup combines dumplings of minced sardine seasoned with miso together with daikon, carrot, and taro root. The umami unique to a blue fish's minced flesh dissolves into the broth along with the depth of miso, and the root vegetables add a mealy texture. It warms the body through, a welcome bowl on a cold day and a fixture of the winter table, now also served in school lunches and enjoyed across generations.

## How it's made
Sardines are filleted, coarsely minced, then ground further in a mortar; grated mountain yam, beaten egg, and miso are worked in. Daikon and carrot are brought to a boil in a pot, taro is added, and the ground sardine is shaped into dumplings with two spoons and dropped in to simmer. When the dumplings float, they are done; soy sauce is added to finish the seasoning, and green onion is scattered on top just before the heat is turned off, so the soup reaches the table while still steaming.

## Why it took this shape
Kujukuri Beach has long landed sardines in huge quantities, a fish so central to the table it is said to have been likened to "rice of the sea." Using every bit of the blue-backed sardine at its fattiest in winter is said to have given rise to this way of shaping the minced fish into dumplings for soup, a winter staple passed from parent to child and still carried on in home kitchens and school lunches today.

sources.title: いわしのだんご汁 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
酢漬けにしたイワシを、豆腐づくりで出るおからで漬け込んだ料理だという。おからの白さが卯の花に似ることから名がついたと伝わり、ピーマンや人参、しょうがの彩りと歯ざわりが加わる。さっぱりとした酸味とおからのほのかな甘みが調和する、日持ちのよい常備菜として日々の食卓に重宝され、正月や祭りにも欠かせない一品とされる。

## どう作るのか
下処理したイワシに塩を振って一日おき、塩を洗い流してから酢と砂糖にさらに一日漬け込む。炒ったおからに酢と砂糖を混ぜ、千切りにして塩もみしたピーマンと人参、みじん切りのしょうがを合わせる。最後に柚子の皮の千切りを加えて和え、香りを立たせながら仕上げ、ひと晩ほど冷蔵庫で冷やして味をなじませてから食べる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
水揚げされたイワシを新鮮なうちに酢漬けにし、さらにおからで包み込むことで型崩れを防ぎ酸化を抑える工夫が生まれたと伝わる。大量に獲れるイワシを無駄なく保存する必要と、豆腐づくりで出るおからを活用する知恵が結びつき、正月や祭りにも用いる保存の利く常備食として、地域の暮らしの中に広く根づいてきたとされる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Vinegar-cured sardines are packed in okara, the soy pulp left from making tofu. The dish is said to take its name from how the white of the okara resembles a certain small white blossom, and bell pepper, carrot, and ginger add color and crunch. The refreshing tartness balances the faint sweetness of the okara, making a long-keeping side dish prized at the everyday table and indispensable at New Year's and festivals alike.

## How it's made
Cleaned sardines are salted and left for a day, then rinsed and cured for another day in vinegar and sugar. Roasted okara is mixed with vinegar and sugar, then combined with julienned, salted bell pepper and carrot along with minced ginger. Julienned yuzu peel is folded in last to bring out the aroma, and the dish is chilled in the refrigerator overnight so the flavors settle before eating.

## Why it took this shape
Sardines were cured in vinegar while still fresh off the boat, and wrapping them further in okara is said to have developed as a way to keep the fish from falling apart and to slow oxidation. The need to preserve a huge catch of sardines without waste combined with the wisdom of putting the okara left from tofu-making to use, and the result is said to have taken root widely in local life as a long-keeping staple served at New Year's and festivals.

sources.title: いわしの卯の花漬け 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
もち米に皮をむいてすりおろした里芋や塩、ごま、のりなどを混ぜ込んでついた餅を薄く切り、乾かしてから油で揚げたり炭火で焼いたりする菓子だという。かりっとした歯ざわりと、じんわり広がる香ばしさが特徴で、揚げてから一か月ほど置いたころが食べごろとされ、素朴なお茶うけとして年間を通して各家庭で親しまれてきた。

## どう作るのか
蒸したもち米にすりおろした里芋や塩、ごま、のりなどを合わせて餅つき機でつき、かまぼこ型にのばす。二日ほどおいて硬くなったら二、三ミリの厚さに切り分け、二日ほど陰干しするか風通しのよい場所で乾かす。半月ほどおいてしっかり乾いたら、低温の油でじっくり揚げるか炭火で焼いていただき、揚げると芯が残らずほどよく膨らむ。

## なぜこの形になったのか
旧暦の正月に餅をつく際、あわせて薄く切って乾かした餅をつくり、日持ちさせて長くお茶うけにしてきたことに由来すると伝わる。里芋を加えるのは地域の畑作物を無駄なく使う工夫とされ、乾燥させて網袋に入れておけば一年近くもつという保存性の高さが、正月の餅を長く楽しむための知恵になったとみられ、今も冬支度の一つとされる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Steamed glutinous rice is pounded together with peeled, grated taro, salt, sesame, and nori, sliced thin once formed, dried, and then either deep-fried or grilled over charcoal into a snack. It is prized for its crisp bite and the toasted aroma that spreads slowly, said to taste best about a month after frying, and it has long been a simple year-round tea companion in local households.

## How it's made
Steamed glutinous rice is combined with grated taro, salt, sesame, and nori and pounded in a rice-cake machine, then shaped into a loaf. After about two days it firms up and is sliced two to three millimeters thick, then air-dried in the shade or a well-ventilated spot for about two days. Once fully dried after roughly half a month, it is either deep-fried slowly in low-temperature oil or grilled over charcoal; frying makes it puff up evenly without a raw core.

## Why it took this shape
It is said to trace back to rice cakes made alongside the New Year's pounding under the old lunar calendar, sliced thin and dried so they would keep and could serve as a tea snack for a long time. Adding taro is said to be a way of using the region's field crops without waste, and the fact that a dried batch kept in a mesh bag lasts nearly a year is thought to have made this a way of stretching New Year's rice cakes further, still part of the winter preparations today.

sources.title: かき餅 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
イワシとおからを酢や味噌で和えた酢の物だという。祝い事のときはウサギの形にととのえて大皿に盛り、そうでないときは俵型に握って盛りつけるなど、場に応じて形を変える。ピーナッツの香ばしさと柚子の香りが加わり、さっぱりとした後味に仕上がる、行事にも日常にも寄り添う一品として今もなお広く長く親しまれ続けている。

## どう作るのか
味噌、酢、砂糖、ピーナッツパウダーを混ぜ合わせ、塩でしめたイワシを酢で洗って細かく切る。油抜きした油揚げを醤油と砂糖で甘辛く煮て、千切りの人参と薄切りのきゅうりは塩でしんなりさせてから水気を絞る。空煎りしたおからにすべての具材を加えて和え、柚子の皮を添えて一人分ずつ俵型に握り、大皿に並べて供することで見栄えよく仕上げる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
行事の膳では一人分ずつ俵型やウサギの形に握って供えるなど、祭りにふさわしい見た目に整えられてきたと伝わる。天然痘を鎮めるための祭りで振る舞われてきた歴史があり、大量に獲れるイワシと豆腐づくりで出るおからを組み合わせることで、行事食と日常食を兼ねる一皿として、家庭ごとに少しずつ形を変えながら受け継がれてきたとされる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Sardine and okara are dressed with vinegar and miso into this vinegared dish. For celebrations it is shaped into a rabbit on a large plate, and on other occasions it is formed into small oval mounds, changing shape to suit the occasion. Toasted peanut and yuzu aroma round it out into a refreshing finish, a dish equally at home at festivals and on the everyday table, still widely enjoyed today.

## How it's made
Miso, vinegar, sugar, and ground peanut are mixed together, and salted sardine is rinsed in vinegar and finely chopped. Fried tofu is blanched, then simmered sweet and savory in soy sauce and sugar; julienned carrot and thin-sliced cucumber are salted until softened and then squeezed dry. All the ingredients are folded into dry-roasted okara, garnished with yuzu peel, shaped by hand into individual oval mounds, and arranged on a large plate to serve.

## Why it took this shape
At festival meals it is said to have been shaped by hand into individual mounds or a rabbit form, dressed up to suit the occasion. It carries a history of being served at a festival held to ward off smallpox, and combining sardines caught in abundance with okara left over from tofu-making is said to have made it a dish that serves both festival and everyday needs, carried on with slight variations from household to household.

sources.title: からなます 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
牛の初乳を火にかけ、酢を加えて固めた豆腐状の食品だという。搾りたての乳ならではの濃厚なこくがあり、日本の伝統的なチーズの一種として食べられてきた。醤油をかけていただくと、乳のまろやかさと醤油の塩気が引き立て合う味わいになり、地域によって呼び名も製法も少しずつ異なり、今も酪農家の間で大切に食べ継がれている。

## どう作るのか
牛乳を沸騰させないよう火にかけて温め、酢を少しずつ回し入れる。水分と豆腐状の部分に分離してきたら火を止め、ざるにあけて水分をよく切る。仕上がったものに醤油をかけて食べるのが基本で、加熱しすぎると分離がうまくいかないため、火加減と酢を加えるタイミングの見極めが求められる、手間と経験のいる作業とされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
産後の牛から出る初乳は傷みが早く一般には流通しないため、酪農家の間だけで食べ継がれてきた食品だったと伝わる。江戸時代に始まったとされるこの地域の酪農の暮らしと結びつき、余った初乳を無駄にしない知恵として、豆腐に似た形に固める食べ方が家々で根づいたとされ、今も地元ならではの味として大切に受け継がれている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Cow's colostrum is heated and set with vinegar into a tofu-like food. It carries the rich depth unique to freshly drawn milk and has been eaten as a kind of traditional Japanese cheese. Drizzled with soy sauce, the mellowness of the milk and the saltiness of the sauce bring each other out, and both the name and the method vary a little by area, still carefully carried on among dairy farming families today.

## How it's made
Milk is heated gently, kept below a boil, while vinegar is poured in little by little. Once it separates into curd and whey, the heat is turned off and the mixture is drained in a colander until the liquid is well removed. It is typically eaten with soy sauce drizzled on top; overheating keeps the separation from working properly, so judging the heat and the timing of the vinegar is a task said to take care and experience.

## Why it took this shape
A cow's colostrum spoils quickly and rarely reached the general market, so it is said to have been eaten only among dairy farming families. Tied to the region's dairy-farming life said to date from the Edo period, setting the surplus colostrum into a tofu-like form is said to have taken root in individual households as a way to avoid letting it go to waste.

sources.title: チッコ豆腐 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
甘辛く煮た豚バラ肉と油揚げをご飯に混ぜ込んだおにぎりで、館山市に伝わる郷土料理だという。ほろりとほどけるご飯に、こってりとした豚肉の旨みと油揚げの甘みが染み込み、片手で頬張れる食べやすさが持ち味とされる。秋祭りで神輿を担ぐ若衆に振る舞われる、力の出る一品として今も親しまれ、日常食としても食べられている。

## どう作るのか
豚バラ肉と油揚げを醤油と砂糖で甘辛く煮て、炊きたてのご飯に混ぜ込む。神輿の担ぎ手が片手で食べられるよう、おにぎりの形ににぎって配られてきた習わしが今も続いている。具をしっかり煮込んでから混ぜるため、汁気が少なくご飯がべたつきにくく、崩れずに持ち運びやすい仕上がりになり、時間がたっても味が落ちにくい。

## なぜこの形になったのか
旧暦十月に出雲へ向かう安房国の人々が、道中の安全を祈って出発前に食べたことに由来すると伝わる。のちに秋祭りで神輿を担ぐ若衆にふるまわれるようになり、片手でつまめるおにぎりの形が定着したとされる。具材をしっかり火を通してから混ぜることは、暑さの残る祭りの時季に食べても傷みにくくする工夫でもあり、理にかなった調理法といえる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This rice ball mixes sweet-and-savory simmered pork belly and fried tofu into rice, a dish handed down in Tateyama. The rice crumbles softly in the mouth as the rich flavor of the pork and the sweetness of the fried tofu soak through it, and it is easy to eat one-handed. It has long been served to the young men who carry the portable shrine at the autumn festival, prized as a hearty, energizing food and also eaten as everyday fare.

## How it's made
Pork belly and fried tofu are simmered sweet and savory in soy sauce and sugar, then mixed into freshly cooked rice. The custom of shaping it into rice balls so the shrine bearers could eat with one hand continues today. Because the ingredients are thoroughly simmered before mixing, the rice stays dry rather than sticky, holds its shape well for carrying, and keeps its flavor even after some time has passed.

## Why it took this shape
It is said to trace back to people of the old Awa domain who ate it before setting out in the tenth lunar month to pray for safe travel to Izumo. It later came to be served to the young men carrying the shrine at the autumn festival, and the one-handed rice-ball shape is said to have taken root from that use. Cooking the ingredients thoroughly before mixing them in is also a reasonable precaution against spoilage during a festival held in the lingering heat of early autumn.

sources.title: ごんじゅう 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
もち米とうるち米を炊いたご飯と小豆あんを、重箱に一人分ずつ丸めず敷き詰めたぼたもちだという。取り分けて好みの量を食べられるのが特徴で、祝儀ではあん・おこわ・あんの三層、不祝儀ではおこわ・あんの二層に詰め分ける。出産のお祝いに欠かせない一品として、地域の家庭に代々受け継がれ、彼岸や祭りにもつくられている。

## どう作るのか
炊いて蒸らしたもち米とうるち米のご飯を、丸めずにそのまま重箱へ敷き詰め、上から小豆あんをのせる。祝儀と不祝儀で層の順番や数を変えるのが習わしで、重箱に入れず一回り大きなぼたもちを三つ用意する地域もある。丸めずに敷き詰めるだけなので、来客の多い大人数の集まりにも向いており、準備の手間があまりかからない。

## なぜこの形になったのか
一人目の子が生まれて三日目に配る祝いの風習として食べられてきたと伝わる。栄養が必要な産後の母親に、もち米と小豆を使った大きなぼたもちを食べてもらおうとしたことが始まりとされ、小豆には邪気を払うという言い伝えも重なり、祝いの席にふさわしい料理として各地の家庭に広まり、今も三日目の祝いとして定着している。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Rice cooked from a mix of glutinous and non-glutinous varieties and sweet red bean paste are layered into a lacquered box, unrolled and unshaped, rather than formed into individual rice balls. Each diner serves themselves as much as they like, and the box is packed in three layers — paste, rice, paste — for celebrations, or two layers — rice, paste — for a somber occasion. It is an essential dish for celebrating a birth, carried on for generations in local households and also made at equinox observances and festivals.

## How it's made
Glutinous and non-glutinous rice are cooked and steamed, then packed unshaped straight into the box, with sweet red bean paste spread over the top. Changing the order and number of layers for a celebration versus a somber occasion is customary, and in some areas three oversized rice balls are prepared instead of using a box at all. Because it is simply layered rather than shaped by hand, it also suits gatherings with many guests, since preparation takes relatively little effort.

## Why it took this shape
It is said to have been eaten as part of a celebratory custom of distributing this dish on the third day after a first child's birth. The custom is said to have begun as a way to feed a new mother, who needed nourishment during recovery, a large rice cake made with nutrient-rich glutinous rice and red beans, and a belief that red beans ward off misfortune layered onto that purpose, spreading it as a fitting dish for a celebration and establishing it as a third-day tradition still observed today.

sources.title: 重箱入りぼたもち 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
鬼おろし器で粗くおろした大根と人参を、節分の炒り大豆や酒かすとともに煮込んだ料理だという。粗い口当たりの大根と人参に酒かすの香りが溶け込み、素朴でどこか力強い味わいになる。初午の日に小豆ご飯とともにお稲荷様へ供える、行事色の濃い一皿として今も受け継がれ、地域によって呼び名も材料も少しずつ異なっている。

## どう作るのか
大根と人参を鬼おろし器で粗くおろし、鍋でそのまま煮る。煮立ったところへ皮をむいた炒り大豆を加え、砂糖や醤油、みりんで味をととのえる。くずした豆腐と千切りの油揚げ、細かくした酒かすを加え、数時間弱火でじっくりと煮込んで味をなじませ、冷めてもおいしくいただけるように仕上げ、日を置くほど味がまとまっていく。

## なぜこの形になったのか
節分に残った炒り大豆を無駄にしないための料理として広まったと伝わる。ふつうのおろし金ではなく粗くおろせる鬼おろし器を使うのは、大根や人参の食感を残して煮崩れを防ぐためとされる。旧暦で年の変わり目にあたる節分に、邪気払いの願いを込めてつくられてきた料理で、地域ごとに呼び名や材料の配合が少しずつ異なる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Daikon and carrot, coarsely grated with a serrated "oni-oroshi" grater, are simmered together with roasted soybeans left from the Setsubun bean-scattering and sake lees. The coarse texture of the vegetables soaks up the aroma of the sake lees for a simple yet hearty flavor. Offered to the fox deity of a shrine along with red bean rice on the first Horse Day of February, it remains a dish steeped in ritual, its name and ingredients varying a little from region to region.

## How it's made
Daikon and carrot are coarsely grated with the serrated grater and simmered as is in a pot. Once it comes to a boil, peeled roasted soybeans are added, and the seasoning is rounded out with sugar, soy sauce, and mirin. Crumbled tofu, julienned fried tofu, and crumbled sake lees are stirred in, and the pot simmers gently over low heat for several hours until the flavors meld, finishing into a dish that tastes good cold too and comes together even more the longer it sits.

## Why it took this shape
It is said to have spread as a way to use up the roasted soybeans left over from Setsubun without waste. The coarse-toothed grater, rather than an ordinary one, is said to be used specifically to leave texture in the daikon and carrot and keep them from breaking down during simmering. Made around Setsubun — the turn of the year under the old lunar calendar — as a dish carrying a wish to ward off misfortune, its name and mix of ingredients vary somewhat by region.

sources.title: すみつかれ 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
大豆に麦麹を合わせ、なすや新しょうが、みょうがなどの夏野菜を加えて仕込む、おかず味噌だという。野菜のみずみずしい食感と麹の甘み、しょうがの辛みが折り重なり、そのままでご飯のお供や酒の肴になる。夏野菜の収穫にあわせてつくられる、季節感のある味噌として東金市を中心に長く親しまれ、家庭ごとに味加減が異なる。

## どう作るのか
短冊切りにしたなすとしょうがをそれぞれ塩でしんなりさせ、重石をして一晩水分を抜く。みょうがは熱湯にくぐらせてせん切りにする。麦麹と醤油、砂糖を合わせた袋に、水気を切った野菜を加えてよく混ぜ、重石をして涼しい場所に置き毎日かき混ぜる。一週間ほど寝かせると味がなじみ、香りよく食べられるようになり、涼しい季節には二週間ほど寝かせることもある。

## なぜこの形になったのか
遣唐使や渡宋僧が持ち帰った製法が日本各地に伝わったという説がいくつか残っており、麦麹に夏野菜を漬け込む形は各地で共通してみられる。千葉県内では東金市を中心に受け継がれ、夏に収穫される野菜を無駄にせず保存できる知恵として、家庭ごとの味を保ちながら今も仕込まれ続けている、暮らしに根ざした味噌とされる。近隣県にも似た味噌があるという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Soybeans are combined with barley koji and summer vegetables such as eggplant, young ginger, and myoga to make this side-dish miso. The juicy crunch of the vegetables, the sweetness of the koji, and the sharpness of the ginger layer together, making it good on its own over rice or with sake. Tied to the summer vegetable harvest, it has long been prized in the Togane area as a seasonal miso, its flavor varying somewhat by household.

## How it's made
Eggplant and ginger, each cut into strips, are salted until softened and left overnight under a weight to draw out moisture. Myoga is blanched briefly and cut into thin strips. Barley koji, soy sauce, and sugar are combined in a bag, the drained vegetables are added and mixed well, and the bag is weighted down and kept in a cool spot, stirred daily. After about a week the flavors settle and it becomes fragrant and ready to eat, though in cooler weather it is sometimes left to cure for about two weeks instead.

## Why it took this shape
Several accounts hold that the method was brought back by envoys or monks who traveled to China, and the practice of curing summer vegetables in barley koji appears in similar form across different regions. Within Chiba it has been carried on mainly around Togane, said to have taken root as a way to preserve the summer harvest without waste, still prepared today while each household keeps its own flavor — a miso woven into daily life, with related versions also found in neighboring prefectures.

sources.title: 金山寺みそ 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
醤油で甘辛く煮た鶏もも肉を炊きたてのご飯に混ぜるだけの、素朴な混ぜご飯だという。小さく切った鶏肉の旨みが米の一粒一粒に染み込み、簡素ながら満足感のある味わいになる。安産祈願の集まりや豊作を願う行事の折に食べられてきた、八千代市高津地区に伝わる素朴な郷土料理で、子どもから大人まで幅広く人気が高く、家庭の定番となっている。

## どう作るのか
小指の先ほどの大きさに切った鶏もも肉を鍋に入れ、醤油を加えて煮汁がわずかに残る程度までしっかり煮詰める。米一升に対し醤油茶わん一杯という分量が代々伝えられており、炊きたてのご飯に煮た鶏肉を煮汁ごと混ぜ込むだけで仕上がる、手間のかからない料理として広く親しまれ、忙しい日でも短い時間ですぐに仕上げられる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
肉が貴重だった時代、誰にでも行き渡るよう鶏肉を小さく切ったという説や、卵を産まなくなった鶏の肉が硬いため細かく刻んだという説が伝わる。限られた食材を工夫して行事の膳にした知恵が、醤油と米だけのシンプルな配合として今も受け継がれ、忙しい現代の食卓にも欠かさず取り入れられ、学校の家庭科の授業でも扱われる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Chicken thigh simmered sweet and savory in soy sauce is simply mixed into freshly cooked rice, a plain rice dish. The umami of the finely cut chicken soaks into every grain of rice, giving a simple yet satisfying flavor. Eaten at gatherings to pray for safe childbirth and at festivals praying for a good harvest, it is a humble local dish from the Takatsu area of Yachiyo, popular with children and adults alike and a fixture of many households' everyday cooking.

## How it's made
Chicken thigh cut into pieces about the size of a fingertip is put in a pot with soy sauce and simmered down until only a little liquid remains. A ratio of one bowl of soy sauce to a large measure of rice has been passed down through generations, and the dish comes together simply by mixing the simmered chicken, broth and all, into freshly cooked rice — an easy dish that can be finished quickly even on a busy day.

## Why it took this shape
One account holds that the chicken was cut small so that everyone could share it fairly in an era when meat was precious; another holds that it was chopped fine because meat from hens no longer laying eggs tends to be tough. The resourcefulness of turning limited ingredients into a festival dish is said to live on in this simple combination of soy sauce and rice, still a fixture at busy modern tables and even taught in home economics classes at school.

sources.title: 高津のとり飯 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
塩漬けにした地元産のたけのこを、醤油と砂糖、酒で下煮してから卵と小麦粉の衣をまとわせて揚げた天ぷらだという。えぐみや苦みが少ない白いたけのこを使うため、あく抜きの手間をかけずに仕込める。からりと揚がった衣の中で、たけのこのほのかな甘みと歯ごたえが引き立つ一品として、地元で古くから親しまれてきた素朴な揚げ物とされる。

## どう作るのか
塩抜きしたたけのこを七ミリほどの厚さに切り、水にさらしてから醤油と砂糖、酒で煮て下味をつける。味がなじんだら小麦粉と卵で衣をつくり、油できつね色にからりと揚げる。塩漬けで保存しておいたたけのこを使うため、収穫期を過ぎても同じ味わいを再現でき、旬とは違う季節にも同じ手順で食卓に並ぶ、扱いやすい料理とされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
小石や岩の破片を含む粘土質の酸性土壌がえぐみの少ない白いたけのこを育て、あく抜きせずに天ぷらにできる下地になったと伝わる。森林の広がる山あいで採れるたけのこを塩漬けにして保存し、旬を過ぎても天ぷらとして味わえるようにした工夫が、通年食べられる料理として根づいた理由とされ、地域の暮らしに欠かせない一品になった。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Local bamboo shoots, cured in salt, are simmered in soy sauce, sugar, and sake, then coated in an egg-and-flour batter and deep-fried. Because the white bamboo shoots used here carry little bitterness or harshness, they can be prepared without the usual step of parboiling to remove it. Inside the crisp batter, the shoot's faint sweetness and crunch come through, a simple fried dish long enjoyed by locals.

## How it's made
Bamboo shoots desalted from their curing are sliced about seven millimeters thick, soaked in water, then simmered in soy sauce, sugar, and sake to season them. Once the flavor has soaked in, they are coated in a flour-and-egg batter and deep-fried to a golden crisp. Because salt-cured shoots are used, the same flavor can be reproduced well past the harvest season, letting the dish reach the table by the same steps in any season.

## Why it took this shape
A clay-rich, acidic soil laced with pebbles and rock fragments is said to be what grows this white bamboo shoot with so little bitterness that it needs no parboiling before frying. Curing the shoots harvested in the forested hills with salt to preserve them, so they can still be enjoyed fried well after their season, is thought to be why this became a dish eaten year-round, an item indispensable to local life.

sources.title: 塩漬けタケノコの天ぷら 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
味付けしたかつお節を芯にして巻いた太巻きで、切り口が鉄砲の筒に似ていることから名がついたと伝わる。すし飯ではなく普通のご飯を使うのが富津の鉄砲巻きの特徴で、かつお節のおかかおにぎりを細長く巻いたような素朴な味わいになる。海苔の産地ならではの、手早くつくれる巻き寿司として長く地元の人々に愛され続けている。

## どう作るのか
炙った海苔を巻きすの上に広げ、ご飯を薄く敷き詰める。醤油をかけて味をつけたかつお節を芯にして、細く巻き上げる。すし飯を使わないぶん手早くつくれ、片手でも食べやすい太さに仕上げるのがこつとされる。切り分けずにそのまま持ち歩けるようにして弁当箱に詰め、漁の合間にほおばることもあるという、手軽さが身上の巻き寿司とされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
海苔の養殖が盛んな富津の浜では、漁の合間に手早く食べられる携帯食が求められたと伝わる。すし飯を仕込む手間を省き、普通のご飯とかつお節だけで仕上げる簡便さが、漁師の弁当として広まった理由とされる。地元でとれる海苔とかつお節を組み合わせた、漁師の暮らしに直結した巻き寿司として今もなお大切に語り継がれている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This rolled sushi wraps seasoned bonito flakes at its core, said to take its name from how the cut cross-section resembles the barrel of a gun. What sets Futtsu's version apart is that it uses plain rice rather than vinegared sushi rice, giving it the simple flavor of a bonito-flake rice ball rolled long and thin. It is a quick, easy roll unique to a region known for growing nori.

## How it's made
Toasted nori is spread over a bamboo mat and topped with a thin layer of rice. Bonito flakes seasoned with soy sauce are laid as the core, and the roll is wound up thin. Skipping vinegared rice makes it quick to prepare, and the trick is said to be rolling it to a thickness that is easy to eat one-handed. It is sometimes packed whole, unsliced, into a lunch box and eaten between hauls of the net — a roll whose whole point is convenience.

## Why it took this shape
On the shores of Futtsu, where nori farming has long thrived, a portable food that could be eaten quickly between fishing tasks is said to have been needed. Skipping the work of preparing vinegared rice and finishing the roll with plain rice and bonito flakes alone is said to be why it spread as a fisherman's lunch. Pairing locally grown nori with bonito flakes, this roll tied directly to fishing life is still spoken of with affection today.

sources.title: 鉄砲巻き 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
ごぼうや人参、しょうが、れんこんなど繊維質の野菜を、砂糖でじっくり煮詰めて乾燥させた保存菓子だという。噛むとほろりとほどける食感に、素材ごとの香りと砂糖の甘みが重なる。漢方薬に由来する名を持ち、農作業の合間に食べる素朴な甘味として、長らく農家の間で世代を超えて大切に受け継がれ親しまれてきた菓子とされる。

## どう作るのか
繊維の多いごぼうやれんこんは薄く切って下ゆでし、あくのあるものはゆでこぼしてから使う。水と砂糖でゆっくりと煮詰め、仕上げに砂糖をまぶして乾燥させる。大きな缶にまとめて保存しておき、必要なときに取り出して食べる。防腐剤を使わずとも長く日持ちするのが特徴で、農繁期には特に重宝されたと今も広く語り伝えられている。

## なぜこの形になったのか
野菜が豊富に採れる土地で、収穫した根菜を砂糖で煮詰めて日持ちさせる知恵として広まったと伝わる。農繁期の田畑仕事の合間に手早く食べられ力になるおやつとして、保存の利くこの菓子が重宝されたとされる。漢方薬の効能にあやかった名前が、素朴な野菜菓子に受け継がれ、今も地元の味として大切に語り伝えられ続けている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Fibrous vegetables such as burdock, carrot, ginger, and lotus root are slow-simmered in sugar and then dried into this preserved sweet. Each crumbles softly at the bite, layering the aroma of its own vegetable with the sweetness of sugar. Its name traces back to a Chinese herbal remedy, and it has long been cherished across generations of farming families as a humble sweet eaten between rounds of fieldwork.

## How it's made
Fibrous vegetables such as burdock and lotus root are sliced thin and parboiled, with any that carry bitterness blanched first. They are then slow-simmered in water and sugar, finished with a dusting of sugar, and dried. The finished pieces are kept together in a large tin and taken out as needed. Prized for keeping a long time without preservatives, it was especially valued during the busy farming season, as the story is still told today.

## Why it took this shape
In a region rich in vegetables, simmering harvested root vegetables in sugar to make them keep is said to have spread as a practical wisdom. As an energizing snack that could be eaten quickly between fieldwork during the busy season, this long-keeping sweet is said to have been prized. A name borrowed from the effects of a Chinese herbal medicine has been carried along with this humble vegetable sweet, still told and valued as a local flavor today.

sources.title: てんもんどう 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
小麦粉の皮であんを包み、サルトリイバラの葉を下に敷いて蒸したまんじゅうだという。葉の香りがほんのりと移り、素朴な甘さのあんと合わさって夏らしい涼やかな味わいになる。丸くつるりとした葉がまんじゅうを包むのに適しており、夏祭りやお盆などのハレの日に古くから各家庭でつくり継がれてきた、涼を呼ぶ素朴な菓子とされる。

## どう作るのか
小麦粉にふくらし粉と砂糖を混ぜてふるい、水を少しずつ加えて耳たぶほどの柔らかさになるまでこねる。生地を分けて手のひらで広げ、丸めたあんを包んで形をととのえたら、塩漬けにしておいた葉の上にのせて蒸し器で蒸す。あんにはさつまいもやかぼちゃを使うこともあり、家庭によって具材にも少しずつ違いが見られるという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
麦の刈り入れが終わったころに挽いた小麦粉を使ってつくられたことに由来すると伝わる。蒸す際にくっつかないよう、丸くつるつるとした葉を器代わりに敷く工夫が根づいたとされる。人が集まる夏祭りやお盆に、材料を持ち寄ってつくる風習とともに、地域の家庭に代々受け継がれ、今もなお大切につくり続けられているという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Sweet bean paste is wrapped in a wheat-flour skin and steamed on a bed of catbrier leaves. The leaf's fragrance lightly perfumes the bun, joining the plain sweetness of the paste for a refreshing, summery flavor. The round, smooth leaf suits wrapping the bun well, and it has long been made in local households for festive occasions such as summer festivals and the Bon holiday.

## How it's made
Wheat flour is sifted together with baking powder and sugar, and water is added a little at a time and kneaded until the dough is as soft as an earlobe. Portions of dough are flattened by hand, wrapped around a ball of sweet bean paste, shaped, and set on a salt-cured leaf before steaming. Sweet potato or pumpkin is sometimes used for the filling instead, so the filling varies a little from household to household.

## Why it took this shape
It is said to trace back to using wheat flour ground from the grain just after the wheat harvest was finished. Lining the steamer with a round, smooth leaf as a substitute plate is said to have taken root as a way to keep the buns from sticking while steaming. Along with the custom of neighbors bringing ingredients together to make them for summer festivals and the Bon holiday, this has been carried on for generations in local households and is still made today.

sources.title: ばらっぱまんじゅう 千葉県

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
炒った米とゆでた小豆に砂糖を合わせて炊いた料理で、見た目は赤飯に似ているがほんのり甘くパラパラとした食感になる。お盆や祝い事、豊作を願う縁起物として食べられてきた。地域によって「やん米」「やき米」など呼び名が異なり、それぞれの土地の言葉とともに今も世代を超えて大切に語り継がれ、今なお各家庭でつくられているという。

## どう作るのか
米を研いでひと晩水に浸したのち、ざるにあげてさらに数時間浸してから水気を切り、鍋で炒る。小豆は砂糖と水を加えて煮て、そこへ炒った米を加え、弱火で蒸すように二十分ほど置いて仕上げる。炒った米のぱらりとした食感と、小豆のほんのり効いた甘さが組み合わさる、素朴で滋味深い仕上がりになるといわれ続けているという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
お盆の迎え火や送り火の際、燃える藁に向かって唱え言葉とともに米と水をまき、故人を迎え送る習わしと結びついていると伝わる。田植えが終わったあとに残った籾を無駄にしない工夫としても食べられてきたとされ、行事の唱え言葉と日々の暮らしの知恵の両方から生まれた、二つの側面を持つ素朴な米料理として受け継がれてきたとされる。

## What it's made of
Toasted rice and boiled red beans are combined with sugar and cooked together into this dish, which looks like red bean rice but tastes faintly sweet with a light, crumbly texture. It has been eaten at the Bon holiday, at celebrations, and as an auspicious food to pray for a good harvest. Its name varies by area — "yangome," "yakigome," and others — each carried on in the local dialect across generations.

## How it's made
Rice is washed and soaked overnight, then drained and soaked again for several more hours before the water is removed and the rice is toasted in a pot. Red beans are simmered with sugar and water, the toasted rice is added, and the pot is left over low heat, steaming gently, for about twenty minutes to finish. The light, crumbly texture of the toasted rice combines with the faint sweetness of the beans for a simple, deeply savory result, so the telling goes.

## Why it took this shape
It is said to be tied to a custom performed at the welcoming and sending fires of the Bon holiday, in which rice and water are scattered toward the burning straw along with chanted words to welcome and see off the departed. It is also said to have been eaten as a way to use up rice grains left over after rice planting was finished, so this simple rice dish carries two threads at once — one from a ritual chant, one from everyday household wisdom.

## 何でできているか
鶏肉とごぼうを煮込み、たたいた骨を混ぜ込んだ鶏団子を加えた雑炊で、最後にご飯を加えて仕上げる汁物だという。ごぼうの香りと鶏の旨みが溶け出した汁にご飯がふっくらと吸い、体の温まる一杯になる。正月や冠婚葬祭など人が集まる席で食べられてきた、市原市に古くから伝わる素朴で滋味深い郷土料理だと語られ続けている。

## どう作るのか
固めに炊いたご飯を用意し、ごぼうはささがきにする。小さく切った鶏肉とごぼうを鍋に入れ、水またはだし汁を加えて柔らかくなるまで煮る。味噌で味をととのえたら、最後にご飯を加えてひと煮立ちさせて仕上げる。ご飯は固めに炊いておくことで、煮汁を吸ってもべたつかず、雑炊らしい食感に仕上がるといわれ続けているという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
どの農家も鶏を飼っていた暮らしの中で、骨まで無駄なくたたいて団子に混ぜ込む工夫が根づいたと伝わる。祝い事や人寄せの折に鶏をつぶして振る舞う機会が多かったことから、集まりの場にふさわしい一皿として定着し、冬の家庭料理としても日常的に食べ継がれ、今も市原の食卓にしっかりと語り継がれ、冬の定番として受け継がれ続けているという。

## What it's made of
Chicken and burdock are simmered together with dumplings made from minced chicken and pounded bone, and rice is stirred in at the end to finish this soupy rice dish. The rice soaks up the broth, rich with the aroma of burdock and the savor of chicken, into a warming bowl. Served at gatherings such as New Year's and formal family occasions, it is spoken of as a humble, deeply savory local dish long handed down in Ichihara.

## How it's made
Rice is cooked slightly firm, and burdock is shaved into thin strips. Chicken cut into small pieces and the burdock go into a pot with water or dashi and are simmered until tender. Miso is added to season the broth, and rice is stirred in at the end for one last boil to finish. Cooking the rice slightly firm beforehand is said to keep it from turning mushy as it soaks up the broth, giving the dish its characteristic texture.

## Why it took this shape
In a time when nearly every farming household kept chickens, pounding even the bones and working them into dumplings so nothing went to waste is said to have taken root. Because chickens were often slaughtered and served at celebrations and gatherings, this dish is said to have become a fixture for such occasions, and it has also been eaten as everyday winter fare, still spoken of fondly at Ichihara's tables today.
